posts.title: CPCA forecasts weak China NEV retail sales in October as peak season falters
posts.summary:
China's NEV retail sales are expected to come in at 1.07 million in October, down 16.5% year-on-year.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's NEV retail sales are projected to decline 16.5% year-on-year to 1.07 million units in October, signaling a faltering peak season.
Overall passenger car retail sales are expected to drop 28.9% year-on-year, reflecting a broader lack of momentum in the Chinese automotive market.
The CPCA notes that high NEV penetration of 66.9% is failing to offset sluggish demand, with most automakers struggling to meet annual sales targets.

posts.title: Chery considers local production in Canada, plans sales launch in 2027
posts.summary:
Chery is assessing idle capacity at existing plants and exploring partnerships with potential investors.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Chery is actively assessing idle manufacturing capacity in Canada, viewing the market as viable even without access to the United States.
The company is exploring partnerships with local investors to establish production, aligning with its broader strategy to localize manufacturing to bypass trade barriers.

While Canada has opened a quota for Chinese-made EVs, the potential for local production could exacerbate trade tensions with the US, which has signaled opposition to Chinese-brand vehicles entering via Canada.

posts.title: BYD's third-gen Qin Plus to launch on October 27 with larger dimensions
posts.summary:
The third-generation Qin Plus grows to 4,840 mm in length and will add roof-mounted LiDAR.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD will launch the third-generation Qin Plus on October 27, featuring a significant dimensional increase and the addition of roof-mounted LiDAR.
The redesign is a strategic response to declining sales, as the Qin series experienced a 54.71% year-on-year volume drop in the first nine months of 2026.
The new model adopts the updated Dynasty design language, aiming to revitalize the entry-level segment through improved cabin space and advanced intelligent features.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
CHIPS Act $389M to power chips, vertical GaN, materials; Micron's memory roadmap; Nvidia expands supply chain capacity; Tenstorrent raises $1.5B; China NAND fabs; 800V power for AI data centers; Intel advances Arizona fab; China orders +$35B in Nvidia GPUs.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The U.S. Commerce Department is allocating $389 million in R&D funding for power electronics and materials, marking a strategic move to secure domestic supply chains for vertical GaN and ultra-high-purity quartz.
Amkor is significantly scaling its advanced packaging footprint, targeting a fourfold increase in interposer wafer capacity by 2028 to support the growing demand for high-performance computing.
Siemens and Nvidia are integrating agentic AI into 3D-IC design workflows, claiming up to 95% reductions in engineering effort and 50x increases in design iteration capabilities.
Infineon and Nvidia are collaborating on 800V power architectures using GaN-based converters to address the critical power density and efficiency requirements of next-generation AI data centers.

Major memory players Samsung and SK hynix are upgrading their Chinese NAND production facilities to advanced node technologies, signaling a continued focus on high-layer-count memory output despite geopolitical constraints.

posts.title: The Download: testing six tech promises and biotech’s blind spots
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Are we there yet? A reality check on six big tech promises Some seemingly impossible feats are too good to give up on. Decoding a pet’s yowls and yips? Absolutely. Scrubbing…
bullets: MIT Technology Review's 'Impossible' issue evaluates the current progress of six long-promised technologies, including nuclear-powered space travel and exercise-mimicking pills.
The report aims to distinguish between genuine scientific breakthroughs and persistent hype cycles that have kept these innovations 'just around the corner' for decades.
Palmer Luckey’s new startup, Warhound, has secured $200 million in funding to pursue the genetic enhancement of military dogs for explosive detection and troop protection.
The publication highlights the ongoing challenge of media and scientific reporting in identifying 'blind spots' when evaluating high-stakes biotech and tech narratives.
